rationale: I read the complete held EO 9067 text within 7 FR 1407 (the file also contains EO 9066 and other orders; EO 9067 is 'Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to War Agencies', six numbered paragraphs, dated February 20, 1942): it directs Budget Bureau priority classifications and Civil Service Commission transfers, gives transferees reemployment benefits under EO 8973, and supersedes conflicting parts of EO 8973. I read the held EO 9243 text (7 FR 7213, September 12, 1942): paragraph 3 states 'Executive Order No. 8973 of December 12, 1941, and Executive Order No. 9067 of February 20, 1942, are hereby revoked, effective on the fifteenth day following the date of this order; provided that nothing contained in this order shall be construed to affect reemployment rights theretofore acquired by any employee under Executive Orders Nos. 8973 and 9067'. The proviso protects rights already acquired, not continued operation of EO 9067. EO 9695 (1946) later revoked EO 9243 and says nothing reviving EO 9067; EO 9952 and EO 9994 (held) state that the remaining reemployment rights expire, which is corroborative. I did not use the ACT records that rely on APP copies. Catalog note and 1989 snapshot are editorial leads. Provisional NO hypothesis.
